findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation is vulnerable to path traversal attacks because it only strips the directory path using os.path.basename, but does not prevent attacks using relative paths like '..' or '\'. A more robust approach is to validate the filename against a whitelist or use a library like pathlib to handle path manipulation securely. This ensures that only authorized files can be accessed.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks by using a whitelist approach or a library like pathlib
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if not filename or '..' in filename or '/' in filename or '\' in filename: return 'Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename)) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group allows unrestricted SSH access on port 22, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, the ingress rule should be updated to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. This can be achieved by specifying the cidr_blocks attribute in the aws_security_group resource.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The AWS DB instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging by setting 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' will allow the instance to export logs to CloudWatch. This will provide visibility into database events and help with auditing and troubleshooting.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' argument
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier          = "app-db"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  username            = "admin"
  password            = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible = false
  storage_encrypted   = true
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["error", "general", "slowquery"]
}

findings.title: EC2 instance has public IP
findings.description: The EC2 instance has a public IP assigned, which poses a security risk as it can be accessed from the internet. To fix this, the associate_public_ip_address attribute should be set to false. This will prevent the instance from being assigned a public IP address.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the public IP assignment from the EC2 instance resource

findings.title: S3 access logging disabled
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_18 check failed because the S3 bucket resource 'aws_s3_bucket.app_data' does not have access logging enabled, which is a security best practice to monitor and track access to the bucket. To fix this, the logging configuration needs to be set on the S3 bucket resource. This can be done by adding a logging block to the resource definition, specifying the target bucket and prefix for the log files.
findings.fix_hint: Enable S3 access logging by setting the logging configuration on the S3 bucket resource

findings.fix_hint: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket to track changes and prevent data loss

Enabling deletion protection prevents the database from being deleted, even if the Terraform configuration is modified to delete it. This can be fixed by adding the 'deletion_protection' argument to the 'aws_db_instance' resource and setting it to 'true'
findings.fix_hint: Enable deletion protection for the AWS DB instance to prevent accidental deletion

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: ec2:*
findings.description: The current policy allows full EC2 control, which is a security risk. To fix this, the ec2 actions should be restricted to only those necessary for the application. For example, if the application only needs to describe instances, the policy should be updated to only include the ec2:DescribeInstances action.
findings.fix_hint: Remove or restrict the overly permissive ec2 actions in the policy

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: s3:*
findings.description: The original policy allows full S3 access on all buckets due to the wildcard action. To fix this, we restrict S3 actions to specific resources and separate the logs permissions into a different statement. This ensures that only the required S3 actions are allowed on the specified bucket, reducing the attack surface.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict S3 actions to specific resources and remove wildcard access

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance Compromise
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to the EC2 instance via an unrestricted SSH connection, then uses a path traversal vulnerability to read sensitive data. This allows them to escalate privileges and gain full control of the instance.
steps: Step 1: attacker connects to the EC2 instance using finding b76d2d49 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf, gaining initial access
Step 2: this gives them the ability to exploit finding d07a18ec in file src/app.py, allowing them to read sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance by updating the security group in xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf

attack_chains.title: S3 Data Exfiltration
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a dangerous IAM policy to access S3, then exploits a lack of access logging to exfiltrate sensitive data without detection. This allows them to steal critical data without being noticed.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses finding dd6eda68 in file iam/policy.json to access S3, gaining access to sensitive data
Step 2: this gives them the ability to exploit finding fdd097e5 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf, allowing them to exfiltrate data without detection
attack_chains.remediation: Update the IAM policy in iam/policy.json to remove dangerous S3 actions

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance and S3 Data Compromise
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to the EC2 instance via an unrestricted SSH connection and a public IP, then uses a path traversal vulnerability to read sensitive data. This allows them to escalate privileges, gain full control of the instance, and access S3 data using a dangerous IAM policy.
steps: Step 1: attacker connects to the EC2 instance using finding b76d2d49 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf and finding d5e736ff in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf, gaining initial access
Step 2: this gives them the ability to exploit finding d07a18ec in file src/app.py, allowing them to read sensitive data and escalate privileges
Step 3: this gives them the ability to use finding dd6eda68 in file iam/policy.json to access S3, allowing them to exfiltrate sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance by updating the security group in xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf and remove the public IP
